title: Ruth Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ruth chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ruth Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ruth Chapter 3.

questions.question: Who spoke to Ruth about seeking rest for her?
questions.correctAnswer: Naomi
questions.explanation: Naomi, Ruth's mother-in-law, spoke to her about seeking rest for her as stated in Ruth 3:1.

questions.question: What was Boaz doing at night on the threshingfloor?
questions.correctAnswer: Winnowing barley
questions.explanation: Boaz was winnowing barley at night on the threshingfloor according to Ruth 3:2.

questions.question: What did Naomi instruct Ruth to do before going to the threshingfloor?
options: Wash herself, anoint herself, put on her raiment
questions.correctAnswer: Wash herself, anoint herself, put on her raiment
questions.explanation: Naomi told Ruth to wash, anoint herself, and put on her raiment before going down to the floor as told in Ruth 3:3.

questions.question: When was Ruth supposed to reveal herself to Boaz?
options: After he had finished eating and drinking
questions.correctAnswer: After he had finished eating and drinking
questions.explanation: Naomi instructed Ruth not to make herself known to Boaz until he had finished eating and drinking, as stated in Ruth 3:3.

questions.question: What was Ruth to do after Boaz lay down?
options: Uncover his feet and lay down
questions.correctAnswer: Uncover his feet and lay down
questions.explanation: Ruth was to mark the place where Boaz lay down, go in, uncover his feet, and lay down there according to Ruth 3:4.

questions.question: How did Ruth respond to Naomi's instructions?
options: She said she would do all that Naomi said
questions.correctAnswer: She said she would do all that Naomi said
questions.explanation: Ruth agreed to do everything Naomi instructed her as stated in Ruth 3:5.

questions.question: Did Ruth follow Naomi's instructions exactly?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ruth went down to the floor and did according to all that Naomi bade her, as mentioned in Ruth 3:6.

questions.question: True or False: Boaz was angry when he found a woman at his feet.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Boaz was afraid and turned himself when he found a woman at his feet, not angry, according to Ruth 3:8.

questions.question: Who did Ruth identify herself as when Boaz asked?
questions.correctAnswer: Ruth thine handmaid
questions.explanation: Ruth answered Boaz saying she was his handmaid as recorded in Ruth 3:9.

questions.question: What did Ruth ask Boaz to do when she revealed herself?
questions.correctAnswer: Spread his skirt over her
questions.explanation: Ruth requested Boaz to spread his skirt over her because he was a near kinsman, as found in Ruth 3:9.

questions.question: True or False: Boaz praised Ruth for showing more kindness at the end than at the beginning.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Boaz blessed Ruth for showing more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning in Ruth 3:10.

questions.question: Who did Boaz say was a nearer kinsman than himself?
questions.correctAnswer: Another unnamed kinsman
questions.explanation: Boaz acknowledged there was a nearer kinsman than himself according to Ruth 3:12.

questions.question: In Ruth 3, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Go to Boaz and uncover his feet
questions.correctAnswer: Wash thyself and anoint thee
questions.explanation: The first instruction Naomi gave Ruth was to wash herself, anoint herself, and put on her raiment before going down to the floor as per Ruth 3:3.

questions.question: True or False: Boaz told Ruth to keep quiet about her visit to the threshingfloor.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Boaz said, 'Let it not be known that a woman came into the floor,' as stated in Ruth 3:14.

questions.question: What did Boaz give to Ruth before she left for the city?
questions.correctAnswer: Six measures of barley
questions.explanation: Boaz measured six measures of barley and laid it on her before she went into the city, as in Ruth 3:15.

medium.title: Ruth Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ruth Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ruth 3:7, what was Boaz doing before Ruth came to the threshing floor?
options: He had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry
He was working in the fields
questions.correctAnswer: He had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry
questions.explanation: Ruth 3:7 states that Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry before he went to lie down, at which time Ruth came softly and uncovered his feet.

questions.question: In Ruth 3:8, what was Boaz's reaction when he awoke at midnight and found a woman at his feet?
options: He was joyful and welcomed her
He was afraid and turned himself
He ignored her and went back to sleep
He immediately called for the elders
questions.correctAnswer: He was afraid and turned himself
questions.explanation: Verse 8 describes how Boaz was afraid and turned himself when he awoke at midnight and saw a woman lying at his feet.

questions.question: What request does Ruth make to Boaz in Ruth 3:9?
options: To spread his skirt over her as a sign of protection
To give her six measures of barley
To tell her who the nearest kinsman is
questions.correctAnswer: To spread his skirt over her as a sign of protection
questions.explanation: In Ruth 3:9, Ruth asks Boaz to spread his skirt over her, symbolizing his role as a near kinsman and protector.

questions.question: How does Boaz commend Ruth in Ruth 3:10?
options: For her kindness shown more in the latter end than at the beginning
For her bravery to come to the threshing floor
questions.correctAnswer: For her kindness shown more in the latter end than at the beginning
questions.explanation: Boaz blesses Ruth in verse 10 for showing more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, highlighting her continued faithfulness and integrity.

questions.question: What assurance does Boaz give Ruth in Ruth 3:11 about the city’s view of her?
options: They think she is a wealthy woman
They know that she is a virtuous woman
They are unaware of her presence
questions.correctAnswer: They know that she is a virtuous woman
questions.explanation: Boaz encourages Ruth in verse 11 by affirming that all the city knows she is a virtuous woman, giving her confidence in his promise.

questions.question: What does Boaz reveal about the kinsman-redeemer situation in Ruth 3:12?
options: There is a kinsman nearer than him
No one is willing to redeem Ruth
He has already redeemed another woman
questions.correctAnswer: There is a kinsman nearer than him
questions.explanation: Boaz admits in verse 12 that although he is a near kinsman, there is another kinsman who is nearer and has first right to redeem.

questions.question: According to Ruth 3:13, what will Boaz do if the nearer kinsman refuses to redeem Ruth?
options: He will do the part of a kinsman and redeem her
He will ask the city elders to decide
He will leave Ruth to Naomi's care
questions.correctAnswer: He will do the part of a kinsman and redeem her
questions.explanation: Verse 13 explains Boaz’s promise that if the nearer kinsman does not redeem Ruth, Boaz himself will do so, demonstrating his commitment and integrity.

questions.question: What instruction does Boaz give Ruth about secrecy in Ruth 3:14?
options: To tell everyone she meets about the plan
To keep it secret that she came to the threshing floor
To announce it at the city gate
questions.correctAnswer: To keep it secret that she came to the threshing floor
questions.explanation: Boaz instructs Ruth in verse 14 not to let it be known that a woman came into the threshing floor, emphasizing discretion and respect for reputation.

questions.question: What gift does Boaz give Ruth in Ruth 3:15, and what does it symbolize?
options: Six measures of barley as a sign of provision and favor
A new cloak as a symbol of protection
A ring as a sign of betrothal
A loaf of bread as a token of hospitality
questions.correctAnswer: Six measures of barley as a sign of provision and favor
questions.explanation: Boaz gives Ruth six measures of barley in verse 15, symbolizing his generosity and provision for her and Naomi.

questions.question: What does Naomi encourage Ruth to do in Ruth 3:18, and what does this teach about patience and trust?
options: To sit still and wait to see how the matter will fall
To confront the nearer kinsman immediately
To leave the city and seek another husband
To tell the people what happened at the threshing floor
questions.correctAnswer: To sit still and wait to see how the matter will fall
questions.explanation: Naomi advises Ruth in verse 18 to be patient and trust that the matter will be resolved, teaching the virtue of waiting on God’s timing.

questions.question: How does Ruth respond to Naomi’s instructions in Ruth 3:5, and what does this illustrate about obedience?
options: She agrees to do all that Naomi says
questions.correctAnswer: She agrees to do all that Naomi says
questions.explanation: Ruth’s response in verse 5 shows her willingness to obey Naomi completely, illustrating faith and submission to wise counsel.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ruth 3:16, Ruth told Naomi everything the man had done after returning from the threshing floor.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 16 states that Ruth came to Naomi and told her all that the man had done, showing openness and trust between them.

questions.question: True or False: In Ruth 3:17, the six measures of barley were given to Ruth so she could sell them in the city.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 17 clarifies that Boaz gave the barley to Ruth so she would not go empty to her mother-in-law, indicating provision rather than for sale.

questions.question: True or False: Ruth's action of lying at Boaz's feet in Ruth 3:7-8 demonstrates humility and trust in God's provision.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ruth 3:7-8 shows her humble approach and trust that Boaz, as a near kinsman, will act according to God's provision and justice.

questions.question: What does Ruth 3:13 promise will happen if Ruth follows Naomi's instructions to stay the night and wait?
options: If the nearer kinsman redeems her, Boaz will not intervene
Boaz will certainly redeem her regardless of the nearer kinsman
She will have to leave the city the next morning
Boaz will marry her immediately without conditions
questions.correctAnswer: If the nearer kinsman redeems her, Boaz will not intervene
questions.explanation: Verse 13 explains that if the nearer kinsman chooses to perform the kinsman's duty, Boaz will let him do so; otherwise, Boaz will redeem her himself, showing respect for legal order and trust in God's plan.

hard.title: Ruth Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ruth Chapter 3.

questions.question: What condition did Boaz mention about the nearer kinsman in relation to Ruth's redemption?
options: The nearer kinsman must first be willing to redeem her
The nearer kinsman had already refused to redeem her
The nearer kinsman was out of the city
The nearer kinsman was a stranger
questions.correctAnswer: The nearer kinsman must first be willing to redeem her
questions.explanation: Ruth 3:12 explains that there was a kinsman nearer than Boaz, implying that this nearer kinsman must have the first right to redeem Ruth, which relates to the cultural practice of the goel or kinsman-redeemer. This connects to Leviticus 25:25, which establishes the concept of the kinsman-redeemer in Israelite law.

questions.question: What did Naomi instruct Ruth to do after Boaz lay down at the threshing floor?
options: Uncover his feet and lie down
Speak to him openly about marriage
questions.correctAnswer: Uncover his feet and lie down
questions.explanation: Ruth 3:4 states Naomi’s instruction to Ruth to uncover Boaz’s feet and lay down there, a culturally significant act symbolizing a request for protection or marriage. This act foreshadows the role of the kinsman-redeemer and is a literary symbol of submission and hope.

questions.question: How did Boaz describe Ruth’s behavior compared to young women of the city?
options: She showed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning
She was as bold as the others
She was less virtuous than most
questions.correctAnswer: She showed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning
questions.explanation: In Ruth 3:10, Boaz blesses Ruth for showing more kindness later than at the beginning, highlighting her loyalty and virtue, contrasting typical courtship behavior and social expectations of women at that time.

questions.question: What did Boaz give to Ruth when she held out her veil?
questions.correctAnswer: Six measures of barley
questions.explanation: Ruth 3:15 records Boaz giving Ruth six measures of barley, symbolizing provision and blessing. This gift underscores the theme of redemption and provision, similar to God's provision for His people in the wilderness (Exodus 16).

questions.question: How did Ruth respond to Naomi's plan at the beginning of the chapter?
options: She agreed to do all that Naomi said
She refused to go to Boaz
questions.correctAnswer: She agreed to do all that Naomi said
questions.explanation: Ruth 3:5 states that Ruth consented fully to Naomi’s instructions, showing her trust and obedience. This exemplifies Ruth’s character of faithfulness, which is a key theme throughout the book.

questions.question: What was Boaz’s reaction when he found Ruth lying at his feet at midnight?
options: He was afraid and turned himself
He immediately called the city elders
questions.correctAnswer: He was afraid and turned himself
questions.explanation: Ruth 3:8 describes Boaz’s initial fear upon waking and seeing Ruth at his feet, indicating his respect and caution given the cultural norms about propriety and the potential scandal.

questions.question: What did Boaz ask Ruth to keep secret after their meeting at the threshing floor?
options: That a woman came into the floor
That barley was given to her
questions.correctAnswer: That a woman came into the floor
questions.explanation: Ruth 3:14 includes Boaz’s instruction to Ruth to keep secret that she came to the threshing floor, reflecting the cultural sensitivity and need for discretion in their actions.

questions.question: What reason did Naomi give Ruth for sitting still after returning from Boaz?
options: To wait until the matter is resolved
questions.correctAnswer: To wait until the matter is resolved
questions.explanation: Ruth 3:18 shows Naomi advising Ruth to be patient and wait to see how things will turn out, revealing the theme of trust in God’s timing and providence.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage establishes the legal principle of a kinsman-redeemer, which is reflected in Ruth 3?
questions.correctAnswer: Leviticus 25:25
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:25 introduces the concept of the kinsman-redeemer, which is directly relevant to the role Boaz seeks to fulfill in Ruth 3:12-13, linking the cultural and legal background to the narrative.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'kinsman' (גֹּאֵל, go'el) as used in Ruth 3?
options: Redeemer or close relative responsible for family restoration
King or ruler of the city
questions.correctAnswer: Redeemer or close relative responsible for family restoration
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'go'el' (kinsman) in Ruth 3:12 refers to a redeemer who has the duty to protect and restore the rights of a family member, an important cultural and legal role in ancient Israel, highlighting the chapter's theme of redemption.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Ruth 3:13-14 with the instructions to 'lie down' and the secretive meeting at the threshing floor?
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: Ruth 3:13-14 uses foreshadowing through the secretive nighttime meeting and the symbolic act of lying down at Boaz’s feet, anticipating the redemption and marriage themes fulfilled later in the narrative.

questions.question: How does Ruth 3:17 reflect the theme of God's provision seen throughout the Old Testament?
options: Boaz giving barley prevents Ruth and Naomi from going empty-handed
Ruth is told to seek provision from the city elders
Naomi sends Ruth to buy food in the market
Boaz promises to bring food daily
questions.correctAnswer: Boaz giving barley prevents Ruth and Naomi from going empty-handed
questions.explanation: Ruth 3:17 highlights Boaz giving six measures of barley to Ruth so she does not return empty-handed, echoing God's provision themes, such as manna in Exodus 16, showing God's faithfulness to sustain His people.

questions.question: What does the veil that Ruth held out symbolize in Ruth 3:15?
options: A symbol of protection and covering
questions.correctAnswer: A symbol of protection and covering
questions.explanation: In Ruth 3:15, the veil represents a covering, symbolizing Boaz's protection and the covenant of redemption. This imagery connects to the broader biblical theme of God’s protective covering over His people (Psalm 91).

questions.question: True or False: Boaz immediately declared his intent to marry Ruth when she first approached him at the threshing floor.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ruth 3:13 shows Boaz explaining that there was a nearer kinsman who had the first right to redeem Ruth, indicating he did not immediately declare intent to marry her but deferred to the legal process.

questions.question: True or False: Naomi was confident that Boaz would settle the matter of redeeming Ruth promptly.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ruth 3:18 records Naomi’s assurance that Boaz would not rest until he finished the matter that day, showing her confidence in Boaz’s integrity and the redemption process.

theological.title: Ruth Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ruth Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Naomi seek for Ruth according to her opening statement?
questions.correctAnswer: Rest and well-being
questions.explanation: Naomi explicitly says, 'My daughter, shall I not seek rest for thee, that it may be well with thee?' indicating her desire is for Ruth's rest and well-being (Ruth 3:1).

questions.question: What specific action does Naomi instruct Ruth to do before approaching Boaz at the threshing floor?
options: Wash, anoint herself, put on her raiment, and do not make herself known
Prepare food and drink for Boaz
Ask for a blessing from the elders first
questions.correctAnswer: Wash, anoint herself, put on her raiment, and do not make herself known
questions.explanation: Naomi tells Ruth to wash, anoint herself, dress properly, and not reveal herself to Boaz until he finishes eating and drinking (Ruth 3:3). This shows preparation and respect.

questions.question: What is the significance of Ruth uncovering Boaz’s feet and lying down there?
options: It is a symbolic act requesting him to be her kinsman-redeemer
It was a cultural gesture of hospitality
She was seeking protection from enemies
It was a sign of submission to his authority
questions.correctAnswer: It is a symbolic act requesting him to be her kinsman-redeemer
questions.explanation: Ruth uncovers Boaz's feet and lies down, an act that anticipates his role as the kinsman-redeemer, as Naomi said he would reveal what to do (Ruth 3:4). This points to the covenantal responsibility Boaz holds.

questions.question: How does Boaz describe Ruth’s behavior toward young men in his blessing?
options: She showed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning by not following young men
She was cautious but open to marriage proposals
She was shy and reserved around men
She was known for her beauty and charm
questions.correctAnswer: She showed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning by not following young men
questions.explanation: Boaz blesses Ruth because she did not seek young men, whether poor or rich, showing more kindness later than at the beginning (Ruth 3:10). This highlights her virtue and loyalty.

questions.question: What does Boaz acknowledge about the presence of another kinsman?
options: There is a nearer kinsman than himself
He is the only kinsman available
The nearer kinsman has refused to redeem
The nearer kinsman is out of the city
questions.correctAnswer: There is a nearer kinsman than himself
questions.explanation: Boaz admits, 'there is a kinsman nearer than I,' acknowledging another who has the first right to redeem Ruth (Ruth 3:12). This introduces the legal and covenantal complexity in redemption.

questions.question: What does Boaz promise Ruth if the nearer kinsman refuses to redeem her?
options: He will redeem her himself as the LORD lives
He will help her find another husband
He will provide for her but not marry her
He will send her back to Naomi
questions.correctAnswer: He will redeem her himself as the LORD lives
questions.explanation: Boaz declares that if the nearer kinsman does not perform the kinsman’s part, then he will do it as the LORD lives (Ruth 3:13), revealing his commitment and the seriousness of the redemption covenant.

questions.question: How did Boaz demonstrate discretion after Ruth left the threshing floor?
options: He instructed that it not be known a woman had come to the floor
He immediately told the city elders
He sent Ruth away with gifts publicly
He announced his intentions in the market square
questions.correctAnswer: He instructed that it not be known a woman had come to the floor
questions.explanation: Boaz says, 'Let it not be known that a woman came into the floor' (Ruth 3:14), showing his discretion and protecting Ruth’s reputation, which reflects wise and honorable conduct.

questions.question: What does the gift of six measures of barley symbolize in this context?
options: Provision and honor to Ruth for her loyalty
questions.correctAnswer: Provision and honor to Ruth for her loyalty
questions.explanation: Boaz gives Ruth six measures of barley so she will not go empty to Naomi, symbolizing provision and honor for her faithfulness (Ruth 3:15,17). This act anticipates God’s providential care.

questions.question: How does Ruth’s obedience to Naomi’s instructions reflect on the doctrine of sanctification?
options: It shows submission and trust in God’s providential guidance through elders
It demonstrates self-reliance in solving problems
It emphasizes ritual purity as the path to salvation
It highlights the necessity of works for justification
questions.correctAnswer: It shows submission and trust in God’s providential guidance through elders
questions.explanation: Ruth’s compliance with Naomi’s instructions (Ruth 3:5-6) exemplifies sanctification by submitting to wise counsel, trusting God’s providence through community guidance (Philippians 2:13).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Ruth 3:11 and Ruth 3:17 give regarding virtue and divine provision?
options: Virtue is recognized by the community and leads to God’s provision
Divine provision depends solely on human effort
Communal recognition is irrelevant to God’s blessings
questions.correctAnswer: Virtue is recognized by the community and leads to God’s provision
questions.explanation: Ruth is called virtuous by the city (Ruth 3:11) and receives barley to not go empty (Ruth 3:17), illustrating that godly virtue is acknowledged communally and results in God’s provision (Proverbs 3:33).

questions.question: How does Boaz’s role as a kinsman-redeemer prefigure Christ’s redemptive work?
options: Boaz’s willingness to redeem Ruth typologically anticipates Christ’s redemption of the church
Boaz’s physical protection symbolizes Christ’s miracles
Boaz’s marriage to Ruth prophesies Christ’s priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: Boaz’s willingness to redeem Ruth typologically anticipates Christ’s redemption of the church
questions.explanation: Boaz acting as a kinsman-redeemer who rescues Ruth from destitution is a type of Christ’s saving work redeeming sinners (Ruth 3:13), as also seen in Hebrews 9:15.

questions.question: What theological truth about God’s providence is illustrated in Ruth 3:18 with Naomi’s counsel to wait?
options: God’s timing is sovereign and must be trusted patiently
God’s plan is immediate and visible
questions.correctAnswer: God’s timing is sovereign and must be trusted patiently
questions.explanation: Naomi advises Ruth to wait until they see how matters fall because Boaz will not rest until he completes the matter (Ruth 3:18), illustrating God’s providential timing and faithfulness (Ecclesiastes 3:1).

questions.question: Sceptics claim the story in Ruth 3 is merely a cultural tale with no spiritual significance. What does Ruth 3:9-11 actually teach about covenant loyalty and God’s blessing?
options: It teaches that covenant loyalty to God and kin leads to divine blessing and favor
It shows that only social customs govern blessings
It implies blessings are random and unrelated to character
It promotes human merit as the basis for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that covenant loyalty to God and kin leads to divine blessing and favor
questions.explanation: Boaz blesses Ruth for her kindness and loyalty rather than seeking young men, highlighting the spiritual principle that God honors covenant loyalty (Ruth 3:9-11), consistent with Psalm 112:5.

questions.question: What does Ruth’s declaration 'All that thou sayest unto me I will do' (Ruth 3:5) reveal about human response to divine guidance?
options: It shows willing submission to God’s providential direction through others
It indicates blind obedience without understanding
It illustrates human independence from God
It emphasizes ritual compliance over faith
questions.correctAnswer: It shows willing submission to God’s providential direction through others
questions.explanation: Ruth’s readiness to obey Naomi’s instructions reflects a heart submitted to God’s sovereign guidance through community, a key aspect of sanctification (Ruth 3:5; Proverbs 3:5-6).

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by Boaz's promise 'as the LORD liveth' in Ruth 3:13?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness and covenantal assurance
questions.explanation: Boaz swears 'as the LORD liveth,' invoking God’s faithfulness and the certainty of covenant promises, reflecting the divine attribute of steadfastness (Ruth 3:13; Numbers 23:19).
